name: Commercial Pressure Washer
definition: A mobile commercial cleaning machine that uses a pump to deliver water through a rated high-pressure hose, trigger gun, lance and nozzle for surface cleaning within the manufacturer's pressure, flow, temperature and application limits.
includedScope: Mobile cold-water electric and engine-driven commercial pressure washers
Machines within the reviewed IEC 60335-2-79 pressure scope up to 35 MPa
excludedScope: Industrial high-pressure water-jet units above 35 MPa
Fixed wash systems, steam-only cleaners and vehicle wash tunnels
Explosive-atmosphere, cutting, surface-removal or potable-water duties without exact approval
headline: Commercial pressure washer pressure, flow, pump, nozzle and buyer verification
description: This profile separates working pressure from maximum pressure and shows how flow, nozzle, hose, pump, water supply, power and surface limits must be verified as one system.
metaDescription: Commercial pressure washer guide covering pressure, flow, cold-water types, pumps, nozzles, models and procurement checks.
disclaimer: This is an independent category reference, not model-specific operating, surface, chemical, water-system or safety advice. High-pressure jets can cause severe harm and property damage. Confirm the current manual, rated components, water supply, PPE, exclusion zone and local rules before procurement or use.

keyFacts.label: Pressure scope
keyFacts.value: Reviewed IEC safety scope covers rated pressure from 2.5 MPa to 35 MPa for non-traction high-pressure cleaners
keyFacts.evidence: IEC 60335-2-79:2021 states the cited pressure range and covered power systems.
keyFacts.scope: Standard scope; exact model certification and regional adoption must be confirmed.

keyFacts.label: Comparison basis
keyFacts.value: Working pressure and flow should be compared together
keyFacts.evidence: Manufacturer specifications separately publish operating or working pressure, maximum pressure and delivery rate.
keyFacts.scope: Named models and their stated regional configurations.

keyFacts.label: Rated-system boundary
keyFacts.value: Hose, gun, lance, nozzle and connectors must suit the exact machine and pressure-temperature envelope
keyFacts.evidence: Official manuals and included-equipment lists identify model-specific spray-system components.
keyFacts.scope: Exact product number, market and accessory set; no cross-brand compatibility is implied.

systemFlow.name: Water supply
systemFlow.role: Provides water within the machine's pressure, temperature, cleanliness and flow limits.
systemFlow.evidence: Official manuals and specifications state inlet temperature, pressure or filtration requirements.
systemFlow.scope: Named models and stated supply or suction modes.

systemFlow.name: Pressure generation
systemFlow.componentFamily: Motor or engine, pump and unloader
systemFlow.role: Raises water pressure and manages flow or bypass according to the machine design.
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturers identify axial or triplex pumps, piston materials and relief or bypass systems.
systemFlow.scope: Exact machine architecture; marketing material does not establish service life.

systemFlow.name: High-pressure transfer
systemFlow.componentFamily: Rated hose, couplings and trigger gun
systemFlow.role: Contains and controls pressurized water between machine and operator.
systemFlow.evidence: Official documentation specifies hose length and supplied gun or coupling systems.
systemFlow.scope: Only rated components approved for the exact model.

systemFlow.name: Jet formation
systemFlow.role: Converts pressure and flow into the intended spray pattern and impact.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources list fixed, adjustable, rotary or multi-function nozzles by model.
systemFlow.scope: Nozzle orifice, pressure, flow and temperature must match the machine.

systemFlow.name: Runoff and shutdown
systemFlow.componentFamily: Work-zone controls, drainage and pressure relief
systemFlow.role: Controls contaminated water and leaves the system in the manufacturer-directed safe state.
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturer documentation describes automatic pressure relief or total-stop systems; site runoff remains a buyer responsibility.
systemFlow.scope: Named machine functions plus local site controls.

variants.name: Electric cold-water mobile washer
variants.taskScale: Routine commercial work near suitable electrical and water supply
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator controls a tethered hose, gun and lance
variants.spaceConstraints: Circuit, cable, water hose, pressure hose and drainage routes
variants.limitations: Regional voltage, phase, plug and input power can restrict deployment.
variants.evidence: Kärcher, Nilfisk, Bosch and Lavor publish electric mobile cold-water models.

variants.name: Engine-driven cold-water washer
variants.taskScale: Remote or construction work without mains power
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator manages fuel engine, pump and spray system
variants.spaceConstraints: Exhaust, fuel, ventilation, noise and transport controls
variants.limitations: Combustion-engine use may be prohibited indoors or in poorly ventilated areas.
variants.evidence: Lavor publishes engine-driven Thermic 9 L with pump and output specifications.
variants.scope: Named model; engine and local environmental rules must be checked.

variants.name: Compact professional or prosumer electric washer
variants.taskScale: Mobile service work with moderate pressure and flow
variants.operatorRelationship: Manual trolley transport and trigger operation
variants.spaceConstraints: Compact storage but still requires rated utilities and exclusion zone
variants.limitations: Professional branding does not establish continuous-duty rating or suitability for every commercial task.
variants.evidence: Bosch, STIHL and Lavor publish named compact high-pressure models and data.

performanceMetrics.name: Working pressure
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Nominal pressure intended during operation at the stated configuration
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: May be adjustable and must be distinguished from maximum permissible or peak pressure
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not rank machines by maximum pressure when working pressure and flow differ.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official sources separately report operating and maximum pressure.

performanceMetrics.name: Delivery rate
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Water volume available to carry loosened soil and influence rinsing speed
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Rated, minimum and maximum flow may use different conditions
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Compare values at a matched operating boundary, not isolated catalogue maxima.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Manufacturers publish litres per hour or minute for named models.

performanceMetrics.name: Nozzle and spray pattern
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Controls jet angle, impact and coverage at the surface
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Included or optional nozzle sets differ by product code
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: A rotary nozzle can increase local impact and risk without increasing the pump's rated output.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official product pages list model-specific fixed, rotary or adjustable nozzles.

performanceMetrics.name: Inlet water temperature and supply
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Defines utility and pump-seal operating boundaries
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Pressure-feed and suction modes may have different limits
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not assume hot-water compatibility from a cold-water category label.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official manuals publish maximum inlet temperature and supply data.

performanceMetrics.name: Power, phase and duty cycle
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Supports circuit, generator, fuel and operating-window planning
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Input power, engine horsepower and pump speed are not directly comparable
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Power rating alone does not establish continuous commercial duty or cleaning result.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Manufacturers publish electrical or engine values and pump arrangements.

applicationFit.evidence: Manufacturers position named models for automotive, agriculture, industry or machinery cleaning.
applicationFit.scope: Surfaces and components that tolerate the selected pressure, temperature and chemical.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Sensitive seals, bearings, electronics, coatings and labels should be mapped before a trial.
applicationFit.assessment: Use the lowest effective pressure and a documented nozzle-distance process.
applicationFit.basis: Official application positioning and adjustable spray systems.
applicationFit.limitations: No vehicle- or equipment-maker approval is implied.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Obtain asset-manufacturer restrictions and test an inconspicuous representative area.

applicationFit.evidence: Nilfisk and Kärcher position reviewed machines for agricultural and industrial applications.
applicationFit.scope: Outdoor or adequately controlled areas with suitable water supply and runoff handling.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Soil type, biosecurity, chemical use and wastewater controls can dominate equipment choice.
applicationFit.assessment: Design the wash process around contamination control and collection, not only pressure.
applicationFit.basis: Official application evidence plus machine water-flow data.
applicationFit.limitations: This profile does not establish food, animal-health or environmental compliance.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Document contaminants and obtain site-specific wastewater and chemical requirements.

applicationFit.evidence: Lavor positions engine-driven professional models for construction and locations without electrical supply.
applicationFit.scope: Outdoor, ventilated and manufacturer-approved operating conditions.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Transport, exhaust, fuel, noise and hose protection must be treated as part of the work system.
applicationFit.assessment: Engine drive solves power access but creates additional site controls.
applicationFit.basis: Official product architecture and application positioning.
applicationFit.limitations: No indoor or confined-space suitability is established.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Complete an engine-use, fire, ventilation and transport assessment before quotation acceptance.

applicationFit.evidence: Commercial high-pressure cleaners are positioned for varied exterior cleaning tasks.
applicationFit.scope: Surfaces able to tolerate water intrusion, pressure and the selected nozzle.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Mortar joints, sealants, paint, glazing and drainage require separate verification.
applicationFit.assessment: A low-pressure test area and runoff plan should precede production cleaning.
applicationFit.basis: Official general application positioning and jet-system specifications.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Obtain substrate-owner approval and document pressure, nozzle, angle and standoff.

componentStack.name: Pump and unloader system
componentStack.role: Generates and regulates high-pressure water flow.
componentStack.evidence: Manufacturer data identifies pump construction and control systems by model.
componentStack.scope: Family labels do not establish cross-model compatibility or service life.

componentStack.name: High-pressure hose and couplings
componentStack.role: Transfers pressurized water to the trigger gun.
componentStack.evidence: Official sources list hose and coupling packages for named products.
componentStack.scope: No cross-brand or visually inferred fit.

componentStack.name: Trigger gun, lance and nozzle
componentStack.role: Controls discharge and forms the cleaning jet.
componentStack.evidence: Official documentation lists exact spray accessories and operating limits.

componentStack.name: Water inlet and filtration
componentStack.role: Protects the pump and supplies sufficient clean water.
componentStack.evidence: Manufacturer manuals publish inlet limits and filters.

componentStack.name: Motor, engine and power connection
componentStack.role: Drives the pump under the intended duty.
componentStack.evidence: Reviewed product data publishes distinct power systems.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Cleaning result at working pressure, flow, nozzle and standoff
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official specifications distinguish working pressure, maximum pressure and flow.
procurementDecisions.scope: Exact model and representative site surface.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Specify a result-based trial at the lowest effective settings.
procurementDecisions.basis: Jet impact and rinsing depend on the complete hydraulic and nozzle system.
procurementDecisions.limitations: WCB has not independently compared cleaning performance.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Trial representative soil and record pressure setting, nozzle, distance, time and water use.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm rated hose, gun, lance, nozzle orifice, flow and inlet supply.

procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Assuming professional naming proves continuous operation
procurementDecisions.evidence: Manufacturer data publishes power, pump and service features but different duty boundaries.
procurementDecisions.scope: Named machines and quoted supplier support.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Route planning must include setup, water access, thermal stops, hose handling and service intervals.
procurementDecisions.basis: Machine architecture and site utilities determine achieved availability.
procurementDecisions.limitations: No normalized duty-cycle test is available across the reviewed sources.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Request a written duty-cycle statement and service-parts schedule for the exact model.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Verify pump type, motor protection, inlet filter, seals and local service inventory.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Fuel, exhaust, transport and operating environment
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Treating lack of mains cable as universal site suitability
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official Lavor data identifies an engine-driven professional configuration.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Engine drive adds controls that must be costed and supervised.
procurementDecisions.basis: Combustion power changes the site risk and logistics profile.
procurementDecisions.limitations: No confined-space or indoor approval is established.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Complete a written engine-use and fuel-management assessment.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm fuel type, exhaust separation, fire controls, transport restraint and pump oil service.

engineeringChecks.reason: Hose, gun, lance, coupling and nozzle must contain the machine's pressure and temperature.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Verify every component part number and its rated envelope against the exact model.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official manuals and product lists identify model-specific spray equipment.
engineeringChecks.scope: No visual or cross-brand compatibility inference.

engineeringChecks.reason: Insufficient or unsuitable inlet water can affect operation and local water-system compliance.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Measure available flow and pressure and confirm filter, temperature and backflow requirements.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Manufacturer specifications publish inlet limits; local controls are jurisdiction-specific.

engineeringChecks.reason: Jet impact, rebound and water intrusion can injure people or damage sensitive surfaces.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Define standoff, nozzle, barriers, PPE, test area and prohibited targets before work.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official manuals provide operating and safety instructions for named machines.
engineeringChecks.scope: Exact task, surface and local safety rules.

engineeringChecks.reason: Dislodged contaminants and detergents may require collection or controlled disposal.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Document soil and chemical composition and obtain the applicable site discharge requirements.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Manufacturer sources identify detergent systems, while disposal requirements remain site-specific.

standards.name: IEC 60335-2-79:2021
standards.applicability: Safety of high-pressure cleaners without traction drive from 2.5 MPa to 35 MPa, including covered electric, battery, combustion, hydraulic and pneumatic drive systems.
standards.evidence: IEC states the pressure and machine scope and listed exclusions.
standards.scope: Confirm regional adoption, product conformity and exclusions for the exact machine.

standards.name: IEC 62885-5:2018
standards.applicability: Methods for describing characteristic performance parameters of household and commercial high-pressure cleaners and steam cleaners.
standards.evidence: IEC states the standard lists performance parameters for machines within IEC 60335-2-79.
standards.scope: It does not make values from unmatched reporting boundaries directly comparable.

developments.title: IEC high-pressure-cleaner safety edition published
developments.summary: IEC published edition 5.0 of IEC 60335-2-79 and clarified scope for hand-held and battery-operated high-pressure cleaners.
developments.evidence: The IEC catalogue records the edition, date and technical revision summary.
developments.scope: International base standard; regional adoption and product certification differ.

developments.title: IEC pressure-cleaner performance-method standard published
developments.summary: IEC published IEC 62885-5 to list characteristic performance parameters for high-pressure cleaners and steam cleaners.
developments.evidence: The IEC catalogue records the publication scope and date.
developments.scope: Measurement framework, not a product ranking.
